extracted.intended_audience: FTA grantees and subgrantees (public transportation agencies), their legal/administrative staff, and FTA regional offices
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for submitting and evaluating petitions for emergency relief to the Federal Transit Administration's Emergency Relief Docket for calendar year 2024. Includes what to include in petitions, submission routes, timelines for conditional grants, and special rules (e.g., Buy America, charter rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting requirement for consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: All petitions for relief from FTA administrative or statutory requirements must be posted in the docket in order to receive consideration by FTA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The docket is publicly available 24 hours a day, seven days a week, via the internet at https://www.regulations.gov/. Even where alternative submission methods are described, posting in the docket is required for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include agency name and docket number
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Include the agency name (Federal Transit Administration) and docket number FTA-2024-0001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions lacking the agency name and docket number may not be properly associated with the Emergency Relief Docket for 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify grantee and geographic location
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) Identify the grantee or subgrantee and its geographic location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear identification of the entity requesting relief and where it operates to allow FTA to assess applicability and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify legal or policy provision from which relief is sought
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) Identify the section of Chapter 53 of Title 49 of the United States Code, or the portion of an FTA policy statement, circular, guidance document or rule, from which the grantee or subgrantee seeks relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite statutory sections, CFR provisions, policy statements, circular numbers, guidance document identifiers, or specific rule language so FTA can locate the requirement at issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain how requirement limits emergency response
rubrics_metrics.description: (d) Specifically address how a requirement in Chapter 53 of Title 49 of the United States Code, or an FTA requirement in a policy statement, circular, agency guidance or rule, will limit a grantee's or subgrantee's ability to respond to a national or regional emergency or disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual and operational detail showing the causal nexus between the requirement and an impediment to emergency response or disaster operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specify one-time or ongoing relief and time period
rubrics_metrics.description: (e) Specify if the petition for relief is one-time or ongoing, and if ongoing identify the time period for which the relief is requested. The time period may not exceed three months; however, additional time may be requested through a second petition for relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requesting ongoing relief, propose a specific time window (<=3 months) and explain why additional time, if needed, will be sought separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional grant for administrative requirements (3 business days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 49 CFR 601.46, a petition for relief from administrative requirements will be conditionally granted for a period of three (3) business days from the date it is submitted to the Emergency Relief Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTA will review the petition after the three-business-day conditional grant period and any comments; it may contact the petitioner or commenters for more information prior to making a final decision. If FTA does not respond within three business days, the grantee or subgrantee may assume its petition is granted for up to three months until FTA states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision factors for grant or denial
rubrics_metrics.description: FTA's decision will be based on whether the petition meets the criteria for use of these emergency procedures, the substance of the request, and any comments submitted regarding the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTA may consider petition content, relevance to emergency procedures, supporting facts, and public comments; FTA may also contact parties for additional information before deciding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory requirement petitions require written decision (no conditional grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition for relief from statutory requirements will not be conditionally granted and requires a written decision from the FTA Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory waivers follow a stricter process—no automatic/conditional short-term grant; expect a formal written determination from the Administrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buy America waivers procedure and exclusion from docket grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees seeking a waiver from Buy America requirements must follow the procedures in 49 CFR 661.7 and 661.9. Buy America waivers will not be granted through the Emergency Relief Docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the Emergency Relief Docket to request Buy America waivers; follow the separate regulatory procedures in 49 CFR part 661.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three submission avenues
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantee or subgrantee has three avenues for submitting a petition: (1) submit via Regulations.gov for posting in the docket; (2) submit a petition in duplicate (two copies) to the FTA Administrator via U.S. mail or hand delivery, via fax, or via email to Bonnie.Graves@dot.gov, or via U.S. mail/hand delivery to DOT Docket Management Facility; (3) if immediate relief is needed and electronic means are unavailable, contact any FTA regional office or FTA headquarters to request staff submit the petition on the grantee's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Regulations.gov as the primary mechanism for prompt docket posting; retain copies and use alternate delivery channels when necessary. For immediate non-electronic needs, regional offices can submit on behalf of grantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Docket opening notice and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: If FTA determines that a national or regional emergency or disaster has occurred, or in anticipation of such an event, FTA will place a message on its web page indicating the Emergency Relief Docket has been opened and including the docket number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor https://www.transit.dot.gov and Regulations.gov for notices that the Emergency Relief Docket is open and for the specific docket number and posting instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTA posting of decisions and reference to petition number
rubrics_metrics.description: An FTA decision, either granting or denying a petition, shall be posted in the Emergency Relief Docket and shall reference the document number of the petition to which it relates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions will be publicly posted in the docket and will identify the underlying petition by document number for transparency and tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: FTA reconsideration authority
rubrics_metrics.description: FTA reserves the right to reconsider any decision made pursuant to these emergency procedures based upon its own initiative, based upon information or comments received subsequent to the three business day comment period, or at the request of a grantee or subgrantee upon denial of a request for relief. FTA shall notify the grantee or subgrantee if FTA plans to reconsider a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are subject to reopening; parties may provide new information or request reconsideration when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter Rule exception for evacuation/urgent movement
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to FTA's Charter Rule at 49 CFR 604.2(f), grantees and subgrantees may assist with evacuations or other movement of people that might otherwise be considered charter transportation when that transportation is in response to an emergency declared by the President, governor or mayor, or in an emergency requiring immediate action prior to a formal declaration, even if a formal declaration is not eventually made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No petition for relief is necessary to provide evacuation/urgent movement services under 49 CFR 604.2(f). However, if the emergency lasts more than 45 calendar days and the grantee will continue to provide service that would otherwise be considered charter service, the grantee or subgrantee shall follow the procedures set out in this notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory basis for waivers tied to emergency grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal public transportation law at 49 U.S.C. 5324(d) provides that a grant awarded under section 5324, or under 49 U.S.C. 5307 or 49 U.S.C. 5311, that is made to address an emergency shall be subject to the terms and conditions the Secretary determines are necessary, allowing FTA to waive certain statutory as well as administrative requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relief is tied to emergency grant awards under chapter 53, explain how Secretary-determined terms apply; but remember statutory petitions still require written decisions under 49 CFR 601.46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to notify regional office before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: FTA strongly encourages grantees and subgrantees to contact their FTA regional office and notify FTA of the intent to submit a petition to the docket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early coordination with regional offices may facilitate faster handling and ensure FTA staff are aware of imminent petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment handling and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments submitted to the docket are public; agencies review submissions and may choose to redact or withhold certain submissions (or portions thereof). Submitted comments may not be available to be read until the agency has approved them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All comments are considered public and will be posted online once the Transportation Department has reviewed them. Expect possible redaction or brief delay while agency reviews submissions for posting.
